chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When you pray behind an Imam whom you follow, do not recite behind him, whether you hear his recitation or do not hear it, unless it is a prayer in which the recitation is loud and you do not hear it, so recite.

key_terms.يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا: In which it is made loud (referring to loud prayer)

ai.seo_question: When should a follower recite Surah Al-Fatihah behind the Imam in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of recitation behind the Imam, distinguishing between silent (Ikhfa) and loud (Jahr) prayers. It establishes that in loud prayers, the follower recites only if they cannot hear the Imam clearly, while in silent prayers, the follower remains silent behind the Imam regardless of audibility, reflecting the Shia view of following the Imam's recitation as sufficient.
